summary: This project focuses on monitoring and analyzing forest fires in Türkiye using NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellite data from 2020 to 2026. Forest fires are becoming more frequent and difficult to control, making early detection essential for protecting ecosystems and natural resources. The project collects satellite data through NASA FIRMS, filters information for Türkiye, standardizes dates and coordinates, and classifies fire locations. By combining MODIS and VIIRS data, the system provides more detailed and accurate fire monitoring. A dashboard allows users to track fire activity, examine different regions, and analyze fire trends. The project aims to identify high-risk areas, predict potential wildfires, and support better planning. Future goals include developing an early warning system, increasing public awareness, analyzing additional data sources, and creating a mobile application to inform people about fire risks. Overall, the project aims to help prevent disasters through satellite-based monitoring and early intervention.
details:
Our project aims to monitor and analyze forest fires across Türkiye using NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellite data from 2020 to 2026.

The main goal of our project is to bring fire detection data from two different satellite systems together on a single platform. By combining MODIS and VIIRS data, we aim to provide a clearer overview of fire locations and their distribution across Türkiye.

Our platform is designed to display detected fire locations on an interactive map, helping users explore fire activity in different regions and years. Users will be able to examine historical fire data, identify areas where fires have been detected, and better understand the distribution of forest fires over time.

The project uses publicly available NASA satellite data and aims to process and visualize this information through a user-friendly web interface. We use Python for data processing and Visual Studio Code as our development environment.

What makes our project innovative is the combination of MODIS and VIIRS fire detection data in one system. Instead of examining these datasets separately, our platform aims to make them easier to access, compare, and understand.

Our project aims to raise awareness about forest fires, support environmental monitoring, and make satellite-based fire information more accessible. In the future, the platform could be further developed with additional analysis and fire risk assessment features.
